title: Error-aware WISE fits retain a near-1000 K median colour for 20 selected dusty dwarfs
abstract: We test whether measurement error and seasonal offsets explain the hot colour reported for 20 W2-variable dusty dwarfs. We fit published NEOWISE 2014-2024 visit fluxes with errors in both bands. We allow alternating-season intercepts, a 0.01 mag error floor and band-error correlations from -0.5 to +0.5. The median blackbody colour is 1044 K with quoted errors and 1030 K with seasonal offsets and the error floor, against the published 997 K. Nine of 20 stars, including three of seven with field kinematics, reject equal fractional W1/W2 changes under every error model at a stricter Gaussian simulation threshold for the group. Simulations recover the input slope but show poor nominal interval coverage in weak sources. G4466 has a conditional colour of 1609 K, but its fixed-spectrum fit fails with quoted errors. Thus the selected-sample hot colour survives this audit. It does not identify grain composition, location or a dust source. Limits include prior W2 selection, assumed error covariance, no visit-level controls and possible changing blends. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-68bc1cebfd8f; topic astronomy; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: Ordinary and error-aware relative-flux slopes and colour temperatures for 20 selected dusty dwarfs. The error-aware model includes alternating-season intercepts and a 0.01 mag error floor. Orange: field kinematics. Blue: young-like kinematics. Points are conditional estimates, not calibrated temperature measurements.
